name: Acorn Napkin Ring
finished_size: About 6 cm across; acorn about 5 cm tall

yarn.description: Cotton yarn for napkin ring and acorn body
Cotton yarn for textured acorn cap

additional_materials: Small amount of polyester fibre fill
gauge: Gauge is not critical; the finished ring should slide over a folded cloth napkin without stretching.

steps.label: Foundation
steps.text: With rust brown, ch 30. Taking care not to twist the chain, sl st in the first ch to form a ring.

steps.label: Rnd 1
steps.text: Ch 1, sc in the same ch as the join and in each remaining ch around; join with a sl st in the first sc.

steps.label: Rnd 2
steps.text: Ch 1, hdc in the same st as the join and in each remaining st around; join with a sl st in the first hdc.

steps.label: Rnd 3
steps.text: Ch 1, dc in the same st as the join and in each remaining st around; join with a sl st in the first dc.

steps.label: Rnd 4
steps.text: Ch 1, hdc in the same st as the join and in each remaining st around; join with a sl st in the first hdc.

steps.label: Rnd 5
steps.text: Ch 1, sc in the same st as the join and in each remaining st around; join with a sl st in the first sc.

steps.label: Rnd 1
steps.text: With rust brown, make 6 sc in an MR.

steps.label: Rnd 2
steps.text: Inc in each st around.

steps.label: Rnd 3
steps.text: (Sc, inc) 6 times.

steps.label: Rnd 4
steps.text: Sc in each st around.

steps.label: Rnd 5
steps.text: Sc in each st around.

steps.label: Rnd 6
steps.text: Sc in each st around.

steps.label: Rnd 7
steps.text: Sc in each st around.

steps.label: Rnd 8
steps.text: (Sc, sc2tog) 6 times.

steps.label: Stuffing
steps.text: Stuff the body firmly with fibre fill, shaping it into a rounded acorn form.

steps.label: Rnd 9
steps.text: Sc2tog 6 times.

steps.label: Rnd 1
steps.text: With dark brown, make 6 sc in an MR.

steps.label: Rnd 2
steps.text: Inc in each st around.

steps.label: Rnd 3
steps.text: (Sc, inc) 6 times.

steps.label: Rnd 4
steps.text: Working in BLO, hdc in each st around.

assembly: Place the cap over the narrow end of the stuffed body, with the cap's Rnd 4 edge aligned to body Rnd 7. Using the cap tail, sew through each of the 18 cap edge sts and the corresponding body sts; secure the yarn inside the acorn.

Centre the acorn over the joining seam on the outside of the napkin ring, with the cap at the top. Using the body tail or a 30 cm length of rust brown yarn, sew through body Rnds 4-6 and ring Rnds 2-4 several times. Secure on the ring's inside.
finishing: After its final rnd, FO each piece by cutting the yarn and drawing the tail through the final loop. Leave a 15 cm tail on the ring, a 25 cm tail on the body, and a 30 cm tail on the cap.
Weave in the remaining yarn tails on the reverse of the ring and inside the acorn, without pulling the stitches out of shape.
Gently shape the acorn body with your fingers so it sits upright and rounded against the ring.
notes: Work the acorn body and cap in continuous spirals; do not join their rnds. Use a stitch marker to mark the first st of each rnd.
The BLO stitches in cap Rnd 4 create a raised ridge that gives the cap its textured appearance.
The ring is worked in joined rnds to create neat, even edges.
